sources.source: Closure of the May 2026 National Rolling Open Market Review
sources.role: The closure records a supplier-evidence collection and evaluation process. Existing and planned build submissions, future outputs and eligibility uses do not establish present-day selected-parcel orderability or measured speed.

sources.source: Closure of the January 2026 National Rolling Open Market Review
sources.role: NR OMR classifications are subsidy-control and procurement-planning evidence. They mix existing and planned supplier claims and cannot be treated as current selected-parcel coverage without exact current validation.

sources.source: National Rolling Open Market Review May 2026 Request For Information
sources.role: The RFI defines evidence, classification and procurement rules. Supplier submissions and subsidy eligibility are not equivalent to live orderability or measured fixed-broadband performance at a selected parcel.

sources.source: National Rolling Open Market Review January 2026 Request For Information
sources.role: The January RFI is a supplier-evidence and subsidy-targeting specification. Its classification logic and investment plans require later evaluation and cannot independently verify current selected-parcel service.

sources.source: Your right to request a decent broadband service: What you need to know
sources.role: USO thresholds, eligibility and build-cost rules describe a legal request process. They do not prove that a selected parcel currently has service, can order immediately or receives a measured speed.

sources.source: Investigation into BT's compliance with its obligations as a broadband universal service provider
sources.role: The closed enforcement case concerns regulatory compliance and excess-cost methodology. It does not establish current broadband availability or measured performance for any selected parcel.

sources.source: UK home broadband performance, measurement period March 2023
sources.role: The study measures a volunteer router panel and provider-supplied package data. National or panel performance cannot be written as a measurement for a selected parcel outside the tested panel.

sources.source: Latest home broadband performance trends revealed
sources.role: These are aggregate findings from a monitored customer panel and provider data. They are not selected-parcel availability, live orderability or a parcel-specific speed test.

sources.source: Closure of the Release 1B Public Review RFI Consultation
sources.role: The Release 1B closure records historic consultation, mapping validation and procurement steps. It does not verify present-day serviceability or measured speed for current selected parcels.

sources.source: Closure of the Third release of Phase 2 Areas Public Reviews
sources.role: The closure is historic consultation and subsidy-targeting evidence. Lot-level mapped eligibility and procurement next steps do not establish current parcel coverage, orderability or measured speed.

sources.source: Closure of the Public Review request for information - release 3A consultation
sources.role: Release 3A mapping and intervention-area evidence is historic subsidy-planning material and cannot verify present-day selected-parcel serviceability or measured performance.

sources.authority: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology / Building Digital UK
sources.role: The process review evaluates programme design, management information and delivery stages. Hub connections and modelled spillovers do not establish current serviceability or measured speed for surrounding selected parcels.
